related_questions.question: What is the function of the M1 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor?
related_questions.snippet: A Muscarinic M1 Receptor is a type of G protein-coupled receptor that mediates the actions of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine in the brain. It plays a role in synaptic responses and has been implicated in conditions like fragile X syndrome.
related_questions.title: Muscarinic M1 Receptor - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics

related_questions.question: What is the action of the M1 muscarinic receptor?
related_questions.snippet: There are three main ways the action of the receptor can be classified: relay of signal, amplification, or integration. Relaying sends the signal onward, amplification increases the effect of a single ligand, and integration allows the signal to be incorporated into another biochemical pathway.
related_questions.title: Receptor (biochemistry) - Wikipedia

related_questions.question: What is an M1 agonist?
related_questions.snippet: The M1 muscarinic receptor is clinically significant in the central nervous system, and it influences neurologic functions. Muscarinic agonists play an important role in the treatment of Alzheimer disease(AD).

related_questions.question: Where can M1 receptors be found?
related_questions.snippet: The M1 receptor is primarily found in the cerebral cortex, gastric, and salivary glands. [5] M2 receptors are diffusely located in smooth muscle and cardiac tissue. [6] M3 receptors are also present on smooth muscle, gastric, and salivary glands.
